title: Train Window
description: Looking up and out of a local train on a summer afternoon, from a low seat: the sky fills the window, the tree line is a fringe along its bottom edge, and the poles of the line right beside the track pass one at a time, each a dark silhouette that rushes up out of the tree line toward a vanishing point overhead, its crossarms and insulators foreshortened hard against the cumulus at the top of the print. Drag sideways to set the train's speed and direction: the field slides past row by row, each at the speed its distance gives it, the pole, its crossarms and insulators seen from right beneath, smears into a soft bar around its dark core, the hedge and the barn behind it drift, and the cumulus over the far tree line barely move. Every layer is blurred by the same 1/125 s shutter at its own screen speed. Let go and the train coasts down to a crawl.
intent: Genre spec idea 8, Train Window (Natsu, moving): Shinkai's 5 Centimeters per Second and Japanese local-line summer imagery. The gesture is the train's speed; motion parallax and shutter blur follow from each layer's distance (blur = screen velocity x shutter). Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallax#Motion_parallax
sources: Field, hedge, barn and far tree line: HDRI 'Rural Asphalt Road', Poly Haven, by Alexander Scholten, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/rural_asphalt_road (16k .hdr). Reprojected square out of the road: the field onto a ground plane (rectilinear, each row at its distance), the hedge and far tree line as cylindrical strips cut with Depth Anything V2 (tools/depth/depth_hr.py) and a colour key. Shipped as log2 radiance -8..+1.5 in 8 bits with TPDF dither.

Sky: HDRI 'Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Pure Sky)', Poly Haven, by Greg Zaal (sky edits Jarod Guest), CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/kloofendal_48d_partly_cloudy_puresky (8k .hdr), rotated so its sun agrees with the field plate's, baked up to the zenith (tools/depth/bakes/train-window/sky.py).

Poles: 3D model 'Modular Electricity Poles', Poly Haven, by James Ray Cock, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/modular_electricity_poles (2k glTF), preset 01 without its guy wire, scaled to an 11.5 m pole with its crossarms running in depth, lit by the field plate's HDRI and rendered from the train's real viewpoint (1.7 m up, 3.4 m off) at 37 view angles along the track for the head and 13 for the trunk (tools/depth/bakes/train-window/poles_render.mjs, poles.py), so the arms' undersides, insulators and transformer foreshorten as the pole crosses the window. Conductors and drop wires are 3D catenaries projected exactly.
